answer: The simplest trick for remembering someone’s name is to repeat it over and over the whole time you’re with them; once you hear it three to four times, it will stick because repetition alone is enough. You don’t need to think of associations or capture it in a notebook, and you can safely ignore accents, titles, and stylized names—the brain picks up the sound automatically. Skip perusing memory apps, elaborate mnemonics, or rote review cards; instead, just keep saying the name out loud in your head as a way of reinforcing what you’ve already heard. Doing this little verbal act immediately builds a lasting memory, so there’s little benefit to other rehearsal techniques.
